section: SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act 1989 and amendments; Civil Rights Protection Act 1955

accepted.s:
With reference to the Centre's task force report of 31 July 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It proposed enhancement of relief for victims.
2. It recommended counselling and State-level relief cells.
3. It proposed that FIRs and charge-sheets be sent to the concerned authorities within 24 hours.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: The task force report proposed higher relief, counselling, State relief cells, and transmission of FIRs and charge-sheets to the authorities within 24 hours.
accepted.tq: Combine several recommendations and identify the option containing all the correct statements.

accepted.s: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes has advocated which combination of measures in cases involving alleged atrocities against tribals?
o: Counter-FIR scrutiny and protection of the livelihood of dispossessed tribals
Preliminary inquiry before every FIR and transfer of cases to civil courts
Abolition of counter-FIRs and withdrawal of livelihood assistance
Compulsory settlement of cases through village councils and suspension of relief
accepted.x: The NCST has sought scrutiny of counter-FIRs and protection of the livelihood of tribals who have been dispossessed.
accepted.tq: Match the institutional recommendation with the correct vulnerable-group concern.

accepted.s: The Madras High Court has held, in the context of offences under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, that:
o: A preliminary inquiry is mandatory before registration of every FIR.
An FIR may be registered only after approval by the State relief cell.
No preliminary inquiry is required before registration of an FIR.
A preliminary inquiry is required only where a counter-FIR is filed.
accepted.x: The Madras High Court held that a preliminary inquiry is not required before registration of an FIR in such cases.
accepted.tq: Test the judicial position by distinguishing a mandatory preliminary inquiry from direct FIR registration.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the contemporary debate surrounding the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act:
1. Claims of misuse have been raised in the debate.
2. Low conviction rates have also been cited as a concern.
3. Counter-FIRs have been alleged to be used for intimidating complainants.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: The debate includes allegations of misuse, concerns regarding low convictions, and criticism that counter-FIRs may intimidate complainants.
accepted.tq: Use a three-part statement question to separate parallel criticisms from a single-sided view.

accepted.s: The Andhra Pradesh Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act, 1989 is primarily associated with prohibition of which practice?
o: The bonded labour system
The dowry system
The manual scavenging system
The Jogini system
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act, 1989 was enacted against the Jogini system.
accepted.tq: Identify the legislation through its specific social practice rather than through a general rights category.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the significance of the Supreme Court's decision in Sukanya Shantha (2024)?
o: Article 17 applies only to physical exclusion from public wells and temples.
Article 17 bars caste-based purity stigma.
Article 17 permits purity-based distinctions when followed by customary communities.
Article 17 concerns only untouchability imposed by private employers.
accepted.x: The Sukanya Shantha decision held that Article 17 bars caste-based purity stigma, expanding the understanding of untouchability beyond narrow physical exclusion.
accepted.tq: Apply the constitutional provision to the precise form of discrimination identified by the judgment.

accepted.s: A ritual described as post-rally 'shuddhikaran' revived a constitutional debate concerning which of the following?
o: Whether caste-based purity stigma constitutes untouchability
Whether relief under the PoA Act can be paid in cash
Whether Devadasi dedication is a form of bonded labour
Whether political rallies require prior judicial permission
accepted.x: The post-rally 'shuddhikaran' ritual revived the debate over whether caste-based purity stigma falls within the prohibition of untouchability under Article 17.
accepted.tq: Link the practical scenario to the constitutional issue it raises, avoiding unrelated social-law concepts.

accepted.s: A High Court questioned the police in a case where the investigation under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act had changed hands six times. Which additional circumstance led to judicial concern?
o: The accused had been acquitted six times by separate Special Courts.
The case had been transferred to six different High Courts within 60 days.
The investigation had been completed within 24 hours without recording statements.
The investigation had remained pending for 26 months beyond the prescribed 60-day limit.
accepted.x: The High Court noted that the probe had changed hands six times and was delayed by 26 months beyond the 60-day limit.
accepted.tq: Use the paired numerical clues—six transfers, 26 months and 60 days—to identify the correct procedural circumstance.

accepted.s: The 2018 development concerning the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act is commonly described as:
o: The Mahajan judgment followed by the legislative response through Section 18A
The Sukanya Shantha judgment followed by repeal of Article 17
The Devadasi judgment followed by insertion of Section 24A
The Madras High Court ruling followed by abolition of Special Courts
accepted.x: The 2018 episode refers to the Mahajan judgment and the subsequent legislative response through Section 18A of the PoA Act.
accepted.tq: Recognise the linked judicial-development and legislative-response sequence.

accepted.s: Which of the following is the principal rehabilitation-related objective associated with the Andhra Pradesh Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act, 1989?
o: Rehabilitation of government servants dismissed for misconduct
Rehabilitation of only displaced industrial workers
Rehabilitation of persons convicted under the PoA Act
Rehabilitation of Jogini women
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh measure is associated with the rehabilitation of women affected by the Jogini system.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Act's rehabilitation focus from unrelated categories of beneficiaries.

accepted.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh support measure mentioned for 2024–25, free power for Scheduled Caste households is provided up to:
o: 200 units
150 units
300 units
100 units
accepted.x: The measure provides free power up to 200 units for Scheduled Caste households, with an allocation of ₹300 crore for 2024–25.
accepted.tq: Test the exact numerical ceiling and avoid confusing it with the associated budget allocation.

accepted.s: The allocation mentioned for providing free power to Scheduled Caste households in Andhra Pradesh during 2024–25 was:
o: ₹100 crore
₹200 crore
₹300 crore
₹500 crore
accepted.x: An allocation of ₹300 crore was mentioned for free power up to 200 units for Scheduled Caste households in 2024–25.
accepted.tq: Separate the monetary allocation from the electricity-unit limit in a paired numerical fact.
